solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Argument about a king's duty

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for argument wraps the other letters

parts.note: a tiff is a petty quarrel or argument
R is the abbreviation for king (Latin rex)

explanation.surface: A dispute over a monarch's levy on goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a tax or customs levy charged on imports, i.e. a duty.

clue.text: Pads from broken sofa bed abandoned by fellow

indicators.note: broken suggests something smashed apart, so the letters of sofa bed are rearranged once the fellow has gone

explanation.surface: Cushions from a broken sofa bed that a man has left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned by fellow' removes the F from SOFABED before 'broken' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Pad is slang for a flat or home, so pads are dwellings.

clue.text: Entwine leg anticlockwise to some extent being graceless

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Twisting a leg the wrong way round looks clumsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking grace or elegance; an adjective for clumsy or awkward.

clue.text: Shark swimming after us keeping depth right

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the mixed letters hold the abbreviation
swimming suggests moving about, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A shark swimming behind us, staying at the right depth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' turns AFTERUS into FRAUSTE, which goes round D; R follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A shark is slang for a swindler or cheat, someone who defrauds others.

clue.text: Critical moment replacing contents of seriously elasticised fastener

indicators.note: the inside letters of the word seriously are swapped out, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: the crunch is the decisive or critical moment

explanation.surface: A serious, tense moment involving some stretchy fastening.
explanation.walkthrough: Only S and Y, the outer letters of 'seriously', survive; CRUNCH goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrunchy is an elastic band covered in fabric, used to fasten hair in a ponytail.

clue.text: One having doubts to persist mostly eating mushroom

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the fungus goes inside
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: to stick at something is to persist
a cep is a porcini mushroom

explanation.surface: A doubter who keeps on eating mushrooms.
explanation.walkthrough: A cep, also called porcini or penny bun, is a prized edible wild mushroom; 'mostly' and 'eating' are the indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptic is a doubter, someone inclined to question claims.

clue.text: Majestic and grand in honest surroundings

indicators.note: in says the letter for grand is placed within the other word
surroundings confirms that the word for honest encloses the letter

parts.note: real means genuine, honest
G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Something majestic and grand in genuine surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal means like a king or queen, stately and majestic.

clue.text: Person recording Cockney's rejection of girl

indicators.note: Cockney speech drops the H sound, so that letter disappears

parts.note: not her rejects a particular girl

explanation.surface: A Londoner taking notes as a girl is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys famously drop their aitches, so the H goes from NOTHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who notes things down is a recorder of them.

clue.text: He modelled with a bra on — hot stuff!

indicators.note: modelled suggests shaped into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man posing in a bra: what a sight!
explanation.definitionFit: A habanero is a very hot chilli pepper, so literally hot stuff.

clue.text: Reporting old-fashioned chap with great anger

parts.note: cove is dated British slang for a man or fellow
rage is fury, great anger

explanation.surface: A news report about an old-fashioned man who is furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Coverage is the reporting of events by press and broadcasters.

clue.text: Survives times after men became disheartened

indicators.note: after places the word for times at the end, following the other piece
losing its heart means the middle letter of the word goes

parts.note: gents is an informal word for men
by means times in multiplication, as in three by four

explanation.surface: Someone gets through hard times after some men lost heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of GENTS is its middle letter N; 'disheartened' removes it to leave GETS.
explanation.definitionFit: To get by is an idiom for managing or surviving with little.

clue.text: Guard provided meal for revolutionary before death

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the word for provided meal is read backwards

parts.note: to have fed someone is to have provided them with a meal
end means death, the end of life

explanation.surface: A guard who supplied food to a rebel before execution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like a rebel being fed, but with 'for' it signals reading the meal word backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To guard is to protect or defend, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Liberal English group backed rave

indicators.note: backed means run backwards, so the letters for English group are reversed

parts.note: a lot is a group or set of items
to rant is to rave, talk wildly

explanation.surface: A liberal English party supported a rave.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal in the sense of open-minded and accepting of others' views is a synonym.

clue.text: A foul stench around brownish- yellow reception rooms

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters enclose the colour word
foul suggests something messed up, so the letters of stench are jumbled

parts.note: amber is a brownish-yellow colour

explanation.surface: A nasty smell surrounding something yellowish-brown in rooms where guests are received.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foul' reads as describing the smell but is the anagram signal, and 'around' has the jumbled smell wrap the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Antechambers are small outer rooms where visitors wait before being received.

clue.text: Individual people in a state oddly rejected compensation

indicators.note: in says the two words sit inside the remaining letters
with odd letters thrown out, only the even letters of the word survive

parts.note: one means a single, individual thing
men means people

explanation.surface: Individuals in a state where rejection paid off oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the odd letters of STATE leaves T and T; ONEMEN goes between them after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonement is making amends or reparation for a wrong.

clue.text: Youth with cuddly toy under bed is spurned

indicators.note: in a down answer, under puts the toy word below the bed word

parts.note: a boy is a youth
a cot is a child's bed
ted is short for teddy, a cuddly toy

explanation.surface: A boy whose teddy is shoved under the bed is rejected.
explanation.definitionFit: To be boycotted is to be shunned or refused dealings, i.e. spurned.

clue.text: Crowded around the French Resistance, showing support

indicators.note: around means the word for crowded wraps the other letters

parts.note: piled in means crowded in
la is French for the (feminine)
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: People crowding around the French Resistance to back it.
explanation.walkthrough: The French Resistance was the wartime underground; here it splits into 'the French' and 'Resistance'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pillared means having columns, which physically hold up a structure.

clue.text: Own rarest ivy, exotic plant

indicators.note: exotic suggests strange or foreign, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener boasting of owning a rare ivy, an exotic plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Winter savory is a perennial herb of the mint family, a culinary plant.

clue.text: A girl's wandering around European capital city

indicators.note: around means the mixed letters enclose the letter for European
wandering suggests straying about, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: the word girls with its S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: A girl roaming round a European capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' mixes AGIRLS to ALGIRS, which goes 'around' E.
explanation.definitionFit: Algiers is the capital city of Algeria.

clue.text: Dismayed, give up bearing husband after a time

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the letter goes inside
in a down answer, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to sag is to give, bend under weight

explanation.surface: Someone dismayed and ready to quit, enduring a husband for a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SAG to GAS, which is 'bearing' H as GHAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast means filled with horror or shock, dismayed.

clue.text: Firmly holding excerpt from newspaper

definitions.meaning: holding tight as a clip or clasp does
a cutting taken from a newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone gripping a cutting from the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Clips fasten things tightly, and a press cutting is also called by this name.

clue.text: 100 in our money exchanged for last of train fare from Italy

indicators.note: exchanged for means one letter is swapped for another

parts.note: pence are British coins
C is the Roman numeral for 100

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Swapping our cash for a final train ticket's price from Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' looks like a train ticket's price but means food here.
explanation.definitionFit: Penne is a tube-shaped Italian pasta, food from Italy.

clue.text: Mad man at sea has removed top

indicators.note: removing the top means the first letter goes, the top of a down answer

parts.note: a pirate is a man at sea, a seaborne robber

explanation.surface: A sailor who lost his hat is angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Mad in the sense of angry, furious, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: No more energy, almost none

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: nought means nothing, none

explanation.surface: A tired person has no more energy, almost none left.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying it as an exclamation means stop, no more of that.

clue.text: Managed to infiltrate intelligence agency's protective structures

indicators.note: to infiltrate means to get inside, so one word goes inside the agency's letters

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency
ran means managed, as one runs a business

explanation.surface: Someone managed to get a spy into the CIA's defences.
explanation.definitionFit: Skulls are the bony cases that protect the brain, so plural skulls are protective structures.

clue.text: Final value is to be replaced with net

indicators.note: replaced suggests the letters are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: An accountant's last value must be swapped for a net figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventual means happening in the end, ultimate or final.

clue.text: Lad's gained from blade so blunt

parts.note: taking the outer letters, the edges, off the word blade leaves lad

explanation.surface: A boy who got something from a blade so dull it would not cut.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer read as an instruction, cutting the borders off BLADE, gives LAD; 'so' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade without a sharp cutting rim is blunt.

clue.text: Far end of market with old fruit is so far

indicators.note: the far end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: a date is the fruit of the date palm

explanation.surface: A fruit stall at the far end of the market, with old stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Up until now, or so far, is an idiomatic synonym.
